200:
** ἀκρίς**, ίδος, ἡ,
**grasshopper, locust, cricket**, {{LXX+8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.12, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1116, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 555b18, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 174.3, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.41, LXX.Exo.10.4, etc.}}:— _singular_, in collective sense, Men.Prot.{{Refs 4th c.AD+|p.108D.; πολλὴ ἀ. 4th c.AD: Hephaestio Astrologus 1.21.}}

**at the extreme angle**, ἀ. λίθος **corner foundation**-stone, {{LXX+NT|LXX.Isa.28.16, NT.Eph.2.20.}}
205:
** ἀκρο-θίνιον** [θῑ], τό,
{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 282, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.132, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 946b}}; mostly _plural_ **ἀκρο-θίνια** or **ἀκρό-θῑνα**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.41, +others}}: _singular_**ἄκρο-θις**, ἡ, _accusative_ **-θινα**{{Refs 4th c.BC+|“GDI” 2561 D 47 Rüsch (Delph., 4th c.BC)}}: (ἄκρος, θίς):—**topmost** or **best part of heap**; hence, **firstfruits of the field, booty**, etc., offered to the gods, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 109, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.86, 90, +others, Pi.[same place], etc.; ἀ. τῆς Μαραθῶνι μάχης “Michel” 1117 (Delph.)}}; ἀκρόθινα πολέμου, in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.4}}, of the Olympic games, **as founded from spoils taken in war**, compare {{Refs|[prev. work] 10(11).57}}.—Properly _neuter_ _adjective_, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 834 ἀκροθίνια θύη}} offerings **of firstfruits.** Post-{{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, rare in early Prose.}}

211:
** ἀλάβαστος** [ᾰλᾰ-]
or **ἄλᾰβ-στρος**, ὁ (ἡ, variant in **Ev Marc.** 14.3), **globular vase without handles for holding perfumes**, often made of alabaster, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.20, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1053, 5th c.BC: Crates Comicus 15.6, 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 62, 143, etc. (ἀλάβαστος (or -ον)}} is the earlier _Attic dialect_ form, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|“SIG” 102, compare 2nd c.AD: Aelius Dionysius Grammaticus “fragment” 31, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 990}}: _Doric dialect_ _accusative_ _plural_ ἀλαβάστρως{{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Lavacrum Palladis” 15)}}:—_neuter_ ἀλάβαστρον {{NT+3rd c.BC+|“IG” 2.745 B 4, 11(2).161 B 9 (Delos, 3rd c.BC), LXX.2Ki.21.13 (codex A), variant in NT.Mark.14.3}}: _plural_ ἀλάβαστρα or **-τα** {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.114, “Anthologia Graeca” 9.153 (6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus).}}
212:
** ἀλαζ-ονεία**, ἡ,
**false pretension, imposture**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 525a, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.47, etc., compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1127a13, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 23; ὑπ᾽ ἀλαζονείας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 919: in _plural_, [prev. author] “Eq.” 290, 903, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.20}}; **boastfulness**, {{Refs 6th c.AD+|6th c.AD: Procopius Caesariensis Historicus “de Bello Persico” 1.11: _metaphorically_, ἀ. χορδῶν}} their **over-readiness** to sound, opposed to ἐξάρνησις, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 531b}}. [That _penultimate_ is long appears from Ar.[same places], {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 737.]}}

240:
** ἀλλήλων**,
_Aeolic dialect_ and _Doric dialect_ ἀλλάλων, _genitive_ _plural_, dua. ἀλλήλοιν, _Epic dialect_ ἀλλήλοιϊν{{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.65}} _feminine_ **-αιν** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.3.18}} codices: _dative_ ἀλλήλοις, αις, οις, _dual_ ἀλλήλοιν: _accusative_ ἀλλήλους, ας, a, _dual_ ἀλλήλω (_feminine_) {{LXX+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.3.18, cf. LXX.Gen.15.10, +others}}: the _dual_ is rare in Prose: _singular_, κεράμὡ ἁρμόττοντι πρὸς ἄλληλον{{Refs|“IG” 2.1054.59: (reduplicate from ἄλλος)}}:—**of one another, to one another, one another**; hence, **mutually, reciprocally**, used of all three persons, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.62, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.209, etc.: freq with Preps., ἐν ἀλλήλοισι}} among **one another**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.223,etc.; τούτω..ἐν ἀλλήλαισι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 188}}; πρὸς ἀλλήλους, εἰς ἄλληλα, {{Refs|[prev. author] “Pr.” 491, 1086}}; ἐπί, πρὸς ἀλλήλοις, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.389, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 506, “Ag.” 654; ἐξἀλλήλων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.4.23; κύκλὡ καὶ ἐξ ἀλλήλων δείκνυσθαι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Priora” 57b18}}; παρ᾽ ἀλλήλους, -α, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 472c, “Phdr.” 264b}}; ἡ δι᾽ ἀλλήλων δεῖξις **reciprocal** proof, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Priora” 59a32,compare 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 9.89, etc.; μετ᾽ ἀλλήλων 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 953b32; πρὸς αὑτὰ καὶ πρὸς ἄλληλα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus γργ. 451c; ὑπ᾽ ἀλλήλων 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 821 (Wrongly interpreted by Grammars as ἑαυτούς, -ῶν, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.105, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.70, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 1124.)}}

246:
** ἀλλό-φῡλος**, ον,
(φυλή) **of another tribe, foreign,** {{LXX+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 12; frequently in LXX of Philistines, LXX.Judg.14.1, +others}}; in Egypt, **settled in another nome**, {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|“BGU” 419.2 (3rd c.AD)}}; ἐς ἀλλόφυλον.. χθόνα{{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 851; ἄνθρωποι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.102, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 629d; ζῷα}}**alien to man, wild,** {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 3.18, 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Abstinentia - Porphyrii Opuscula” 1.10}}; πόλεμος ἀ. war **with foreigners,** {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Camillus” 23}}; opposed to ὁμόφυλος, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Sententiae” 39; ἀ. πρός τι 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 308; μᾶζαν ἐπ᾽ ἀ.}}**alien, not one's own,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 159.12.}}
251:
** ἅλς**, ἁλός [ᾰ],
h(
**B** (ἁλὸς πολιοῖο{{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.229)}}, **sea** (generally of shallow water near shore), εἰς ἅλα δῖαν{{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.141; χεῖρας νιψάμενος πολιῆς ἁλός}}**in sea-water,** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.261; ἢ ἁλὸς ἢ ἐπὶ γῆς 12.27: sometimes pleonastic πόντος ἁλός 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.59, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 10}}; ἁλὸς πελάγη or πέλαγος, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.335, “hymnus ad Apollinem” 73, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 88; πελαγίαν ἅλα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 427; παρ᾽ ἁλμυρὰν ἅλα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 17}}; in _plural_ (with a pun on ἅλς A), {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 760.—poetical word: _nominative_ only 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 56}}. (Cf. Latin _sal:_ both _masculine_ and _feminine_ are from the same root.)

265:

**failure, fault,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1261 (Lyric poetry)}}; frequently in _Attic dialect_ Prose, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.3.8, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.65, etc.}}; midway between ἀδίκημα and ἀτύχημα, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1135b18, “Rh.” 1374b7}}; **sinful action,** opposed to κατόρθωμα, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Zeno Citieus Stoicus 1.54, compare “PTeb.” 5.3, etc.; τὸ περὶ τὴν τέχνην λεγόμενον ἁ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 296b, compare “Ap.” 22d; εἴς τινα [prev. author] “Lg.” 729e; περὶ τὸ σῶμα [prev. author] “Grg.” 479a.}}

Scholia 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” “Oxy.” 21.203.}}
270:
** ἀμάω**,
**B**mostly _Epic dialect_ in _middle_, **draw, gather** (compare ἐξ-, ἐπ-, καταμάομαι), ταλάροισιν ἀμησάμενοι [γάλα]{{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.247, compare 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.859; ἀλλότριον κάματον σφετέρην ἐς γαστέρ᾽ ἀμῶνται 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 599; ἀμήσατο γαῖαν ἀμφ᾽ αὐτοῖς 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.1305: _metaphorically_, ἀρετήν 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 5.169b:}} —_active_, χερσὶν ἀμήσας κρατὸς ὕπερθε κόνιν, of a mourner, **pouring** dust on his head, {{Refs|“Anthologia Graeca” 7.241 (Antip.).}}—poetical and later Prose.
